newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, MidEast discounts feature.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, MidEast discounts feature.

text.p: Asia crude prices were steady on Thursday in outright terms, but wet differentials remained at a discount for MidEast barrels.
Paper prices were mostly level but the loss of production at Cossack and Griffin owing to a storm was offering underlying support for the light sweet market, traders said.
Two majors traded a Qatar Land cargo at QGPC less 4.5 cents, after a similar deal was heard at QGPC less seven on Wednesday.
A Japanese refiner was heard involved in a Qatar Marine/Murban swap with a European major -- reflecting a similar deal heard on Wednesday also involving the refiner.
But Oman held its recent premium levels -- although traders said they still expected the crude to eventually fall into discount territory given the expected weakness for April trade.
A French major was heard selling an Oman cargo at MPM +4.5 cents, matching a day-earlier deal. It was the second purchase of Oman for the South Korean buyers, traders said.
The 65,000 bpd Cossack and 80,000 bpd Griffin fields off western Australian stopped production earlier on Thursday because of an approaching storm.

Traders said it could prompt a squeeze on April supply of light sweet grades into Australia but trade had not yet started. Light sweet benchmark March Tapis paper was quoted at $22.00/$22.20 and April was at $21.45/$21.60, little changed from a day-earlier.
Indonesia crude was quiet but an initial Minas deal was heard but unconfirmed at ICP +40 cents, matching pre-market expectations.
Traders said the official export allocation of 94,300 bpd would mean further allocations would be made in view of the 38-day shutdown of the Dumai refinery starting on Saturday.
